plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid). In such auctions, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Since there's no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $23 to maximize expected profit.

In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Since my value is $18, I should bid exactly $18 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid). The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value: bidding higher risks overpaying if I win against a bid above my value, and bidding lower only risks losing profitable opportunities without any benefit. Since my value is $25, bidding $25 ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never pay more than my value.
